title: Introduce operator-boundary RBAC shield + KMS region assertor and audit fanout
author: Aisha Patel
description: Background and motivation: several customers reported ambiguous operator-level access where service operator tokens could perform cross-tenant KMS lookups during a paging incident (SUP-711). This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an operator-boundary RBAC shim that enforces RBAC v2 constraints at operator scope (prevents operator-scoped principals from implicitly gaining tenant-scoped capabilities), and (2) a KMS region assertor that validates KMS key usage is compatible with the request's declared region and emits an immutable provenance entry into the audit pipeline. Additionally, an audit fanout path is added so KMS provenance and operator-claim metadata are forwarded to the long-term audit store and to an internal mini-index for fast residency queries. Design summary: - Operator-boundary RBAC shield: new RBAC middleware evaluates an incoming request's operator claim and enforces deny-by-default rules for any tenant-scoped actions. It plugs into RBAC v2 decision flow and exposes a lightweight allowlist for explicitly delegated operator actions. Configuration is via the existing RBAC policy bundles with two new annotations: "operator_scope: true" and "operator_allowed_actions". - KMS region assertor: at KMS call sites, we validate the key's declared region against the request's region/geo-claim. Failures are surfaced as a 403 with a machine-readable audit tag. For compatibility we add a non-blocking "warn" mode toggle controlled by feature-flag rbac.operator_kms_assert_mode (warn|enforce). - Audit fanout: the KMS assertor emits an immutable provenance record (kms_provenance_v1) to the audit writer. The writer has an option to fanout a summarized message to the compliance index (for fast residency checks) and to the long-term blob store. Rollout plan: feature gated behind rbac.operator_boundary flag. Start in warn mode for two weeks for telemetry collection, then opt-in rollouts by account for enforcement. Ops tasks: add alert (rbac.operator_assert_fail_rate > 0.5% per hour) and dashboard panels for "operator_assertions", "kms_provenance_skips", and "audit_fanout_latency_ms". Compatibility and migration: existing RBAC policies remain valid but bundles that intend operator delegation must add the operator_scope annotation. KMS providers that don't surface region metadata will be treated as unknown-region and will be logged; we provide a helper adapter to enrich provider responses. Testing and validation: unit tests for the RBAC decision path; integration tests exercising operator-scoped tokens against tenant actions; end-to-end e2e against local KMS stub verifying audit fanout. Security review: design reviewed by SEC/Privacy and includes threat scenarios for operator privilege escalation, replay attacks on KMS provenance, and audit tampering mitigations. Documentation: updated auth/rbac/README and added a short runbook for incident responders.
